name: New Mexico
headline_status: Recreational cannabis is legal for adults 21+, and New Mexico also runs a medical cannabis program.
summary: New Mexico legalized adult-use cannabis through the Cannabis Regulation Act, with possession and home growing allowed from June 29, 2021 and licensed retail sales starting April 1, 2022. Adults 21+ may carry up to 2 ounces of flower, 16 grams of concentrate and 800 mg of edibles, and may grow at home. The state's medical program dates to 2007. The adult-use excise tax rose from 12% to 13% on July 1, 2025 and is scheduled to climb one point a year until it reaches 18% in 2030.

adult_use_since.value: Possession and home grow legal since June 29, 2021 under the Cannabis Regulation Act.

medical_since.value: 2007, under the Lynn and Erin Compassionate Use Act.

possession_limit.value: Up to 2 oz of cannabis, 16 g of concentrate and 800 mg of edibles in public; larger amounts allowed at home if locked away and not visible from public spaces.

home_grow.value: Six mature and six immature plants per adult, capped at 12 mature plants per household; localities cannot ban home cultivation.

public_use.value: Smoking cannabis in public carries a $50 fine; cities and counties may allow consumption in 21+ locations, and licensed consumption areas are permitted.

taxes.value: Cannabis excise tax rose from 12% to 13% on July 1, 2025, with 1-point annual increases scheduled until it reaches 18% in July 2030; gross receipts tax also applies. Medical sales are exempt from the excise tax.

medical_program.value: Patients with a listed qualifying condition (about 30, including cancer, epilepsy, PTSD and severe chronic pain) can enroll; the Department of Health runs patient registration and patients buy tax-free.

regulator.value: Cannabis Control Division of the New Mexico Regulation and Licensing Department (business licensing for adult-use and medical).

penalties.value: Public possession of more than 2 oz up to 8 oz is a misdemeanor; 8 oz or more is a fourth-degree felony.

dui.value: Impairment-based: New Mexico has no THC per se or zero-tolerance law, so a cannabis DWI requires evidence of impairment. Using cannabis while driving is illegal.

tourists.value: Yes. Adult-use sales are open to anyone 21+ with valid ID, up to 2 ounces of cannabis, 16 grams of concentrate and 800 mg of edibles at a time. Out-of-state patients can enroll as reciprocal participants for medical purchases.

timeline.event: Lynn and Erin Compassionate Use Act creates the medical cannabis program
Cannabis Regulation Act takes effect; adult possession and home grow become legal
Governor signs SB 6, tightening penalties for unlicensed activity and updating licensing rules
Cannabis excise tax rises from 12% to 13%, the first of scheduled annual increases

faq.q: Is weed legal in New Mexico?
faq.a: Yes. Adults 21 and older can legally possess, buy and grow cannabis, and licensed dispensaries have sold to adults since April 1, 2022.

faq.q: How much weed can you carry in New Mexico?
faq.a: In public, up to 2 ounces of flower, 16 grams of concentrate and 800 mg of edibles. More can be kept at home if it is locked up and out of public view.

faq.q: Can you grow cannabis at home in New Mexico?
faq.a: Yes. Each adult may grow six mature and six immature plants, with no more than 12 mature plants per household.

faq.q: Can you smoke weed in public in New Mexico?
faq.a: No. Public smoking can bring a $50 fine, though local governments may allow consumption at designated 21+ locations and licensed consumption areas.
